messages:
olga (Acme IT): Hi team — quick security gating question from our vendor risk group: can Redwood support customer-managed master keys that are HSM-backed? They want details on custody, envelope encryption, rotation cadence, and sample SIG/CAIQ language.

maria (Sales): Thanks Olga — short answer: yes. We support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS integrations or HSM for Private deployments. Looping in Aj and Kevin for the technical + SIG wording.

aj (Solutions Eng): A few specifics: we always use envelope encryption. Data encryption keys (DEKs) are generated by the runtime and encrypted (wrapped) with your CMK. If you enable BYOK/CMK, the CMK remains in your KMS/HSM and we never store unwrapped CMKs or plaintext master keys. In-transit is protected by TLS 1.3.

kevin (Security): For vendor risk reviewers: two supported patterns: 
- Customer KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure KV): grant Redwood a principal that can Wrap/Unwrap or GenerateDataKey as needed.
- HSM/on-prem: PKCS#11 integration or customer-managed KMS; we support HSM-backed wrapping.
Rotation: CMK rotation is controlled by the customer; DEKs are rotated by Redwood on a configurable cadence (default 90 days). All wrap/unwrap events are logged and available in the audit export.

olga (Acme IT): Can you paste sample SIG/CAIQ/CAIQ-friendly language for the matrix? They asked for custody + evidence samples.

aj (Solutions Eng): Sure, here's a copyable snippet you can drop into the CAIQ: 

aj (Solutions Eng): ```
Encryption: Data at rest is protected using AES-256-GCM. Per-tenant data encryption keys (DEKs) are generated and used for data encryption; DEKs are wrapped by customer-managed master keys (CMKs) held in the customer's KMS/HSM. Redwood does not persist plaintext CMKs or unwrapped master keys. In-transit encryption is enforced with TLS 1.3. Key usage and wrap/unwrap events are captured in audit logs and can be exported to the customer's logging backend for review.```

kevin (Security): Addendum for CAIQ: we can provide KMS ARNs, rotation timestamps, and signed rotation proofs for PII-impacting keys. We can also run a short demo showing HSM-backed wrapping and audit evidence if the vendor team requests.

maria (Sales): Note on pricing and procurement: enabling BYOK/HSM options for Dedicated/Private may affect the SOW and cost. Recommend a 2-week technical PoC: validate key integration + one model endpoint. Want us to propose a SOW?

olga (Acme IT): Yes please. Also need a checklist for our infosec to sign off and SLA text for key operation latency (they care about wrap/unwrap response times).

aj (Solutions Eng): I'll prepare a PoC checklist. Basic items: KMS ARNs, service principal/IAM role, allowed KMS actions, network egress IPs, and sample config. Example snippet for AWS: 

aj (Solutions Eng): ```yaml
redwood_kms:
  provider: aws
  cmk_arn: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-1234
  role_arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/RedwoodWrapRole
  allowed_actions: ["kms:GenerateDataKey","kms:Encrypt","kms:Decrypt","kms:ReEncryptTo"]
```

kevin (Security): SLA note: key ops are synchronous; typical wrap/unwrap latencies against managed KMS are ~10-30ms. For on-prem HSM we include a short-lived DEK cache to avoid tail latencies. Full details and failover behavior will be spelled out in the SOW.

olga (Acme IT): This is great — can you attach the SIG/CAIQ text and the checklist when you send the SOW? Our vendor risk team will want the exact wording.

maria (Sales): Will do. I'll assemble: 1) SIG/CAIQ text, 2) PoC checklist, 3) high-level SOW outline including SLA language and pricing variance for BYOK/HSM. Expect it in the next few hours.

infra-bot: Docs uploaded: https://redwood.docs/internal/kms-integration (permissions: sales,security)

olga (Acme IT): Awesome, thanks all :raised_hands:
